areas.name: Trou aux Biches and Mont Choisy
Belle Mare and Trou d'Eau Douce

places.name: La Cuvette Beach
places.blurb: A small public beach on the north-west edge of Grand Baie, quieter than the main bay and popular with families.
places.speech: La Cuvette is a small, quiet public beach on the edge of Grand Baie.

places.name: Grand Baie La Croisette
places.blurb: Grand Baie's large shopping mall, with fashion and home stores, an Intermart hypermarket, sit-down restaurants and a food pavilion.
places.speech: La Croisette is Grand Baie's big shopping mall, with shops, a hypermarket and plenty of places to eat.
places.notes: Open every day, per the official site.

places.name: Notre-Dame Auxiliatrice Church, Cap Malheureux
places.blurb: A small red-roofed church at the northern tip of the island, facing the islet of Coin de Mire; inside, the holy-water basin is a giant clam shell.
places.speech: The little red-roofed church at Cap Malheureux, near Grand Baie, looks out over the sea to Coin de Mire.

places.name: Trou aux Biches Beach
places.blurb: A north-west beach shaded by casuarina trees, with a calm lagoon for snorkelling, dive schools close by and good sunsets.
places.speech: Trou aux Biches beach has a calm lagoon for snorkelling and lovely sunsets.

places.name: Mont Choisy Beach
places.blurb: A long curve of white sand lined with casuarinas between Trou aux Biches and Grand Baie, with calm, clear water for swimming and snorkelling.
places.speech: Mont Choisy beach is a long stretch of white sand with calm water, good for a swim.

places.name: Maheswarnath Mandir
places.blurb: Founded in 1888 in Triolet, this Shiva temple complex is the largest Hindu temple in Mauritius, with several smaller shrines and colourful sculptures.
places.speech: Maheswarnath Mandir in Triolet is the largest Hindu temple in Mauritius, dedicated to Shiva.

places.name: Mont Choisy Le Mall
places.blurb: A lifestyle shopping centre at Mont Choisy with a supermarket, small boutiques of local products, delicatessens and Italian, Japanese and Indian restaurants.
places.speech: Mont Choisy Le Mall has a supermarket, small shops and restaurants, close to Trou aux Biches.

places.name: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Botanic Garden
places.blurb: A historic botanic garden in Pamplemousses, famous for its pond of giant water lilies, its many palms and spice trees, and resident giant tortoises.
places.speech: The Pamplemousses botanic garden is famous for its giant water lilies, palm trees and giant tortoises.

places.name: L'Aventure du Sucre
places.blurb: A museum inside an old sugar mill at Beau Plan that tells the island's story through sugar, ending with tastings of sugarcane products and rum.
places.speech: L'Aventure du Sucre is a museum in an old sugar mill near Pamplemousses, with tastings at the end.
places.notes: Open Monday to Saturday, including public holidays, per the official site.

places.name: Château de Labourdonnais
places.blurb: A restored 19th-century colonial mansion in the north, with period furniture, an underground museum, gardens and tastings of the estate's rums, juices and jams.
places.speech: Château de Labourdonnais is a restored colonial mansion with a museum and tastings of its own rums and juices.

places.name: Port Louis Central Market
places.blurb: The capital's busy market hall, piled with tropical fruit and vegetables, with local crafts on the first floor and kiosks selling dholl puri and alouda.
places.speech: Port Louis Central Market is a lively covered market with fruit, crafts upstairs and local street food.

places.name: Le Caudan Waterfront
places.blurb: A harbourside complex in Port Louis, open since 1996, with shops, cafés, restaurants, a cinema, an arts centre and the Blue Penny Museum.
places.speech: Le Caudan Waterfront in Port Louis has shops, restaurants, a cinema and a museum, right on the harbour.

places.name: Blue Penny Museum
places.blurb: A museum at Le Caudan Waterfront covering Mauritian history, old maps and art, home to the famous Mauritius Post Office stamps and a Paul and Virginie sculpture.
places.speech: The Blue Penny Museum at Le Caudan shows the island's rare Post Office stamps, old maps and art.
places.notes: Closed on Sundays and public holidays, per the official site.

places.name: Natural History Museum, Port Louis
places.blurb: The oldest museum in Mauritius, in the Mauritius Institute building, best known for its dodo skeleton, alongside birds, shells, insects and geology displays.
places.speech: The Natural History Museum in Port Louis is the island's oldest museum, best known for its dodo skeleton.
places.notes: Open weekdays and Saturday mornings, per the Mauritius Museums Council.

places.name: Aapravasi Ghat
places.blurb: World Heritage remains of the immigration depot where hundreds of thousands of indentured labourers, mostly from India, arrived after slavery was abolished.
places.speech: Aapravasi Ghat in Port Louis is the World Heritage depot where indentured workers first arrived in Mauritius.

places.name: Odysseo Oceanarium
places.blurb: An indoor oceanarium on the Port Louis waterfront with around 300 marine species, shark and stingray encounters, and a focus on ocean conservation.
places.speech: Odysseo is an indoor oceanarium in Port Louis with sharks, rays and hundreds of sea creatures.
places.notes: Last entry is at 4:15 pm, per the official site.

places.name: Eureka House
places.blurb: A colonial mansion in Moka from around 1836, built of local hardwoods and now a museum with period furniture, set in gardens with small waterfalls.
places.speech: Eureka is a colonial mansion museum in Moka, with period furniture and gardens leading down to waterfalls.

places.name: Bagatelle Mall
places.blurb: A large mall in Moka with more than 150 stores, a food market and restaurants, a cinema, bowling and an indoor play area for children.
places.speech: Bagatelle Mall in Moka has over a hundred and fifty shops, a cinema, bowling and plenty of food.

places.name: Le Pouce
places.blurb: A climb to the 812-metre thumb-shaped summit between Moka and Port Louis, with a rocky final scramble and wide views; Charles Darwin went up in 1836.
places.speech: Le Pouce is a half-day hike to a thumb-shaped peak with sweeping views over Port Louis.
places.notes: Start early to avoid the heat, per Mauritius Now.

places.name: Trou aux Cerfs
places.blurb: A dormant volcanic crater in Curepipe, about 80 metres deep with a small lake at the bottom; the 605-metre rim gives wide views over the island.
places.speech: Trou aux Cerfs is a forested volcanic crater in Curepipe with views across the island from its rim.

places.name: Domaine des Aubineaux
places.blurb: A colonial house built in 1872 at Forest Side, Curepipe, now a museum, with the Maison des Essences, a floral park and a restaurant serving Mauritian food.
places.speech: Domaine des Aubineaux is a colonial house museum in Curepipe, with gardens and a restaurant.

places.name: So'flo
places.blurb: A smaller, calm shopping centre in Floréal, near Curepipe, with fashion stores, a supermarket, cafés, restaurants and a spa over two floors.
places.speech: So'flo in Floréal, near Curepipe, is a calm shopping centre with shops, cafes and restaurants.

places.name: Grand Bassin (Ganga Talao)
places.blurb: A sacred crater lake in the southern uplands ringed by Hindu shrines, with a 33-metre Shiva statue at its gateway; it is the focus of the Maha Shivaratri pilgrimage.
places.speech: Grand Bassin is a sacred Hindu lake in the hills, watched over by a giant statue of Shiva.

places.name: Flic en Flac Beach
places.blurb: About eight kilometres of white sand on the west coast, shaded by casuarinas, with a warm lagoon for snorkelling and street-food stands nearby.
places.speech: Flic en Flac beach is one of the longest on the island, with a calm lagoon and street food nearby.

places.name: Casela Nature Parks
places.blurb: A large wildlife park at Cascavelle with an African safari area, big cats, giraffes, rhinos, aviaries, a petting farm and a children's play park.
places.speech: Casela, near Flic en Flac, is a big wildlife park with giraffes, lions, rhinos and a petting farm.
places.notes: Open daily 9 am to 5 pm except 25 December and 1 January, per the official site.

places.name: Cascavelle Mall
places.blurb: The west coast's main shopping centre at Cascavelle, just inland from Flic en Flac, with groceries, fashion and home stores, restaurants and a food court.
places.speech: Cascavelle Mall, just inland from Flic en Flac, has shops, a supermarket and a food court.

places.name: Black River Gorges National Park
places.blurb: The island's largest national park, with more than 50 kilometres of trails through rainforest and valleys, endemic birds and Black River Peak, the highest summit.
places.speech: Black River Gorges National Park has rainforest trails, waterfalls and rare birds in the hills above Black River.

places.name: Martello Tower Museum
places.blurb: A British coastal defence tower from the 1830s on La Preneuse beach, restored as a museum and shown on guided tours of its rooms and rooftop cannon.
places.speech: The Martello Tower in La Preneuse is a restored British fort from the eighteen thirties, seen on a guided tour.

places.name: Tamarin Bay
places.blurb: A wide west-coast bay long known to surfers, where spinner and bottlenose dolphins are often seen early in the morning and dolphin-watching boats set out.
places.speech: Tamarin Bay is a surf spot where dolphins are often seen in the early morning.

places.name: Seven Coloured Earth Geopark
places.blurb: Small dunes of naturally striped sand in shades from red and brown to violet and yellow, in a park that also has a tortoise enclosure and waterfall viewpoints.
places.speech: The Seven Coloured Earth in Chamarel is a patch of striped dunes in seven shades of sand.
places.notes: Open every day, including Sundays and public holidays, per the official site.

places.name: Chamarel Waterfall
places.blurb: One of the island's highest waterfalls, dropping about 100 metres over a basalt cliff into a pool, seen from two viewpoints inside the geopark.
places.speech: Chamarel Waterfall plunges about one hundred metres down a basalt cliff, seen from viewpoints in the geopark.
places.notes: Its two viewpoints are included in the geopark entrance ticket, per the official site.

places.name: Rhumerie de Chamarel
places.blurb: A rum distillery in Chamarel offering guided visits that follow the spirit from cane harvest to bottle, with its own restaurant, L'Alchimiste.
places.speech: Rhumerie de Chamarel is a rum distillery in Chamarel with guided tours and a restaurant.

places.name: Ebony Forest
places.blurb: A non-profit reserve in Chamarel bringing back native forest, with walking trails, guided conservation tours, endemic birds and lookouts over the south-west coast.
places.speech: Ebony Forest in Chamarel is a restored native forest with trails, rare birds and coastal viewpoints.

places.name: Alexandra Falls Viewpoint
places.blurb: A signposted lookout in Black River Gorges National Park, on the plateau road east of Chamarel, with views of Alexandra Falls and the forested gorges.
places.speech: The Alexandra Falls viewpoint in Black River Gorges National Park looks over a waterfall and forested gorges.

places.name: Le Morne Brabant
places.blurb: A 556-metre basalt mountain on the south-west tip, a World Heritage cultural landscape and a symbol of the escaped slaves who once sheltered on it.
places.speech: Le Morne Brabant is a World Heritage mountain, remembered as a refuge for people who escaped slavery.

places.name: Le Morne Beach
places.blurb: White sand and coconut palms at the foot of Le Morne Brabant, known for its sunsets and its kitesurfing, including the famous One Eye spot.
places.speech: Le Morne beach sits beneath the mountain, with white sand, kitesurfers and great sunsets.

places.name: Île aux Bénitiers
places.blurb: An uninhabited islet in the lagoon north of Le Morne, with white sand and a small coconut farm, plus snorkelling across to the clam-shaped Crystal Rock.
places.speech: Île aux Bénitiers is a little island in the Le Morne lagoon, reached by boat, with snorkelling at Crystal Rock.
places.notes: Local fishing boats leave from La Gaulette or Case Noyale, per Mauritius Now.

places.name: Gris Gris
places.blurb: A wild stretch of the south coast by Souillac where huge waves pound the shore below the clifftops, with the rocks of La Roche Qui Pleure close by.
places.speech: Gris Gris, near Souillac, is a wild clifftop where huge waves crash against the south coast.
places.notes: Not for swimming: strong currents and big waves, per Mauritius Now.

places.name: Rochester Falls
places.blurb: A 10-metre waterfall about 2.5 kilometres from Souillac, spilling over a cliff of jagged, block-shaped rock into a pool where people swim and picnic.
places.speech: Rochester Falls, near Souillac, tumbles over striking blocks of rock into a natural pool.
places.notes: Avoid during or after heavy rain: rocks get slippery and water rises, per Mauritius Now.

places.name: Bois Chéri Tea Estate
places.blurb: The island's oldest tea plantation, in the southern hills, with guided tours of the tea factory and its museum, followed by a tasting of Bois Chéri teas.
places.speech: Bois Chéri is a tea estate in the southern hills with a factory tour, a tea museum and a tasting.

places.name: Domaine de Saint Aubin
places.blurb: A colonial estate near Rivière des Anguilles with a guided house visit, a rum house with tastings, a vanilla house, gardens and a Mauritian restaurant.
places.speech: Domaine de Saint Aubin is a colonial estate near Souillac with rum tastings, vanilla and gardens.

places.name: La Vanille Nature Park
places.blurb: A wildlife park in a valley at Rivière des Anguilles, home to more than 1,000 Aldabra giant tortoises and 2,000 Nile crocodiles, plus a fossil museum.
places.speech: La Vanille Nature Park, near Souillac, has more than a thousand giant tortoises and lots of crocodiles.
places.notes: Open every day 9 am to 5 pm, including public holidays, per the official site.

places.name: Blue Bay Marine Park
places.blurb: A protected lagoon south of Mahébourg with a brain-coral garden and reef fish; wade in from Blue Bay beach to snorkel, or view it from a glass-bottom boat.
places.speech: Blue Bay Marine Park is a protected lagoon near Mahébourg, great for snorkelling or a glass bottom boat trip.

places.name: Île aux Aigrettes
places.blurb: A coral-ringed islet off Mahébourg, a nature reserve since 1965, where guided tours show restored coastal forest, pink pigeons and giant tortoises.
places.speech: Île aux Aigrettes is a nature reserve island off Mahébourg, visited on guided tours to see rare birds.
places.notes: Visits are guided EcoTours of about 1.5 to 2 hours, per the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation.

places.name: Mahébourg Market
places.blurb: Mahébourg's traditional market, with aisles of stalls under corrugated roofs; it is at its liveliest on Monday, the big market day.
places.speech: Mahébourg market is a lively covered market, at its busiest on Mondays.
places.notes: Arrive before 8 am on Monday market day, per a 2026 Westimmo guide.

places.name: Biscuiterie Rault
places.blurb: A family business just north of Mahébourg that has baked cassava biscuits over a wood fire for more than a century; visits end with a tasting and Mauritian tea.
places.speech: Biscuiterie Rault in Mahébourg is a family biscuit factory where you can taste cassava biscuits with tea.
places.notes: Booking is advised in high season, per a 2026 Westimmo guide.

places.name: Bo'Valon Mall
places.blurb: A shopping mall on the edge of Mahébourg, a few minutes from the airport, with fashion and home stores, a supermarket, a food court and a children's play area.
places.speech: Bo'Valon Mall, near Mahébourg, has shops, a supermarket and a food court under one roof.

places.name: Île aux Cerfs
places.blurb: An uninhabited island off the east coast, reached by boat shuttle, with white-sand beaches, a lagoon for water sports, beach bars and a championship golf course.
places.speech: Île aux Cerfs is an island off the east coast, reached by boat, with white beaches and a calm lagoon.
places.notes: Boat shuttles leave from Pointe Maurice, per Mauritius Now.

places.name: Belle Mare Beach
places.blurb: One of the island's longest beaches, with around ten kilometres of white sand on the east coast, casuarina shade and clear water for swimming and snorkelling.
places.speech: Belle Mare beach is a long stretch of white sand on the east coast, lovely for an early swim.

places.name: Central Flacq Market
places.blurb: One of the biggest markets in Mauritius, an open-air sprawl of fresh produce, clothes, souvenirs and street food in Centre de Flacq, inland from Belle Mare.
places.speech: Central Flacq market is a huge open-air market inland from Belle Mare, full of produce and street food.
places.notes: Busiest on Wednesdays and Sundays, when all stalls open, per Mauritius Now.
